proposed_fix.description: Verify whether socket/connection exhaustion on productcatalogservice or its node (e.g. conntrack pressure) is causing the latency, then relieve it with gated, reversible actions.
steps: Inspect socket state on the productcatalogservice pod(s): count of ESTABLISHED/TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT connections and open file descriptors, compared with the pre-incident baseline.
Check node conntrack usage (nf_conntrack_count vs nf_conntrack_max) on the node(s) hosting productcatalogservice to confirm or rule out R1.
Identify which clients hold the most connections to productcatalogservice (e.g. recommendationservice, frontend) and check whether they are leaking or not reusing connections.
If conntrack is near its limit, request approval to raise nf_conntrack_max on the affected node as a temporary measure.
If connections are leaking in a specific client, request approval for a rolling restart of that client deployment, one replica at a time, watching latency-50/90 and the socket metric.
Keep investigating the CPU rise (z=50.63) in parallel, since E4 shows it also deviated, to see whether it is a cause or a side effect of connection churn.
preconditions: Confirm the socket metric deviation is still present at action time and not a transient spike.
Confirm conntrack usage is actually high before touching sysctl settings; otherwise skip that step.
Confirm there is spare capacity in the client deployments before any rolling restart.
Get explicit human approval for every change to the node or a deployment.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restore nf_conntrack_max to its previous recorded value, and if a rolling restart makes things worse, stop it and redeploy the previous revision with kubectl rollout undo; no other state is changed.
